areas.title: Men's market: Hiko for men and other men's services
areas.question: Is there an untapped men's market worth a separate men-only test ad set, and what would the advisor run?
areas.headline: Fix the leak first (₱65k* a month already goes to men through women-led ads), then a small men-only test: ₱600/day before VAT for 21 days, Jawtox and Hiko for men, judged by bookings per chat.

findings.text: Nov 2024 to Nov 2026: men took 25.4% of Hermosa ad spend (₱2,664,422*) and gave 24.2% of chats (55,633) at ₱47.9* per chat, vs women ₱44.9*. No ad was ever made for men; they saw women-led ads.
findings.source: Hermosa Meta accounts via Windsor, gender breakdown

findings.text: Clients are about 90% women (CHRIS). So a man who chatted was about a third as likely to become a client as a woman who chatted, and each male client cost about 3x as much in ads.
findings.source: Hermosa Meta accounts via Windsor + CHRIS Nov 28

findings.text: Last 30 days: men still got ₱65,205* (about 21%) and 1,733 chats, even in ad sets named 'Women only', because Advantage+ audience treats gender as a suggestion.
findings.source: Hermosa Meta accounts via Windsor, ad set x gender

findings.text: Reaching men is cheap (₱58* per 1,000 views vs ₱102* for women), so a men-only test must be judged by bookings per chat, not cost per chat.
Men's services already on the menu: diode laser beard ₱999, upper neck ₱599, lip ₱499. No men's Hiko package or men's ad exists.

No clinic in QC, Fairview, Marikina or Bulacan advertises Hiko for men. Men's lines exist only in BGC/Pasig (Aivee Masculook, Lift, BroVage) and lead with the jaw. Hiko Deluxe ₱8,999 is below QC rivals (₱9,999-10,599).

PH clinics report more men: Glow Skin about 1 in 10 clients (2018) to 4 in 10 (2025); Lift about 55%. Owner estimates from BGC/Pasig, not our area. Men want discreet, natural results; 'retokado' stigma remains.
Ads must not imply the viewer's looks ('Malaki ba ilong mo?' is out; 'Sharper jawline, natural pa rin' is fine). Gender is a hard limit only with original audience options.

areas.recommendation: 1) Make every regular ad set women only as a hard limit and close 'All Genders + Mid class filter' (stops about ₱65k* a month to men). 2) Then, with your OK: one men-only ad set at QC Main, own campaign, gender Men, original audience, ages 21-54, ₱600/day before VAT for 21 days (₱12,600). Two male-led Taglish ads: Jawtox, and Hiko for men with ₱8,999/₱13,999. No before/after, no women in the ads. Front desk tags chats MEN-TEST. Win = men's bookings per chat at least 0.7x the women's at the same branch and 5+ paid treatments; below 0.4x = stop for good.
areas.next: Waiting for your OK on the women-only fixes (they're on This week's moves). The men's test waits until those are done.

areas.title: Philippine market data only
areas.question: Is US market data right for PH ads advice? What PH data can we use instead?
areas.headline: US figures removed. The advisor now uses our own numbers first, then PH clinic prices, then PH Meta costs.

findings.text: Our cost per chat 2026: QC ₱43.9*, Fairview ₱45.1*, Sta. Maria ₱39.0*, Marikina ₱38.5*. Winners ₱19.5-33.7*.
PH Hiko prices: budget ₱5,000-6,999, mid-market ₱10,599-11,999, premium from ₱35,000. Deluxe ₱8,999 sits below mid-market; Ultra Max ₱13,999 fills the gap to premium.
PH Meta: median CPM about ₱87, CPC about ₱4.70, cost per message ₱15-50 (agency range).

areas.recommendation: Keep PH-only evidence in every ads decision.

areas.title: Past Meta ads: what paid back
areas.question: Which past ads, branches and services returned the most sales per peso?
areas.headline: 2026 average 5.1x ROAS, but extra money in the same ads returned only 0.5-1.8x. Growth comes from new offers, not bigger Hiko budgets.

findings.text: 2026 ROAS by page: QC 4.9x, Fairview 4.3x, Sta. Maria 5.5x, Marikina 6.8x. Hiko took 85% of spend.
findings.source: Hermosa sales + Meta spend by page

findings.text: QC Main halved spend in November and sales held, the only real natural test.
findings.source: Hermosa sales + Meta spend by page

findings.text: More chats did not bring more sales: QC sales per chat fell from ₱370 (Apr) to ₱155 (Aug-Sep).
findings.source: Hermosa sales + Meta spend by page

areas.recommendation: Don't raise existing Hiko budgets for growth; put new money into Ultra Max, the Botox family and NovoForm.

areas.title: Bring Fairview back to #2
areas.question: Why did Fairview fall from the #2 branch, and what brings it back?
areas.headline: Fairview logs ₱0 sales on 5-8 days a month (often Wednesdays). Fixing those days and a Fairview-only Hiko reset are the first steps.

findings.text: 2023: ₱927k a month, #2 every month. 2026 Jan-Oct: ₱399k a month, #2 only in October.
19 of 60 ₱0-sales days in 2026 were Wednesdays; QC Main has 1-2 such days a month.
Fairview Hiko returns 2.8x, the weakest branch and service.
findings.source: Hermosa sales + Meta spend by page

areas.recommendation: Fix ₱0 days, CSR weekday fill, Fairview-specific Hiko ads, budget FV Hiko ₱60k + FV drips ₱15k a month (pre-VAT). Targets: Dec ₱550k, Mar 2027 ₱650k a month.
areas.next: Watch December sales against the ₱550k target.

areas.title: Sales gaps and expansion by service and branch
areas.question: Which services sell well with little or no ad money behind them, and where would extra budget pay back?
areas.headline: Ultra Max (₱348.5k), the Botox family (₱151k) and NovoForm (₱31k) sold in Nov 1-24 with no ads behind them. Three tests take ₱1,900/day before VAT out of the old test budget.

findings.text: Ultra Max: 25 clients and ₱348,500 in Nov 1-24, which is 27% of Hiko clients and 37% of Hiko money, yet no ad ever led with it. It only needs 1.8% of chats to buy for 5x ROAS.
Botox family (Jawtox, Botox, Barbie arms, Sweatox): ₱151,000 from 28 clients with 0% of ad spend. Fairview and Marikina sold ₱0 of Jawtox.
NovoForm: ₱31,000 from 4 clients (Fairview ₱25.5k). Its old static ads got chats at ₱17-29*, the cheapest of any service.
Hiko Deluxe/Pro gets about 90% of spend. QC Main halved its spend in November and sales held, so more money in the same Hiko ads is not where growth is.
findings.source: Hermosa Meta by page + declared sales

findings.text: Week to week, extra spend returned only 0.5-1.8x (correlation -0.2 to 0.2). QC sales per chat fell from ₱370 (Apr) to ₱155 (Aug-Sep), so chat quality and closing are the limit, not chat volume.
findings.source: Hermosa Meta by page + declared sales, 45 weeks of 2026 (playbook/branch-month-2026.csv)

findings.text: Marikina has the best return per peso (6.7x) and is the only branch where spend shows a hint of paying back 2 weeks later.
findings.source: Hermosa Meta by page + declared sales

areas.recommendation: With your OK: 1) Ultra Max ad set at QC Main, ₱1,000/day before VAT. 2) Botox family across all 4 branches, ₱600/day. 3) NovoForm at Fairview + QC, ₱300/day. These are funded from the old test budget, so the total stays about ₱363k a month before VAT. 4) Marikina Hiko +20% for 3 weeks as a controlled test. Every ad set is women only.
areas.next: Waiting for your OK on the 3 tests and the Marikina raise (Sales: Manage Meta ads thread). Each change goes to you as a preview first.

areas.title: When to refresh or turn off an ad
areas.question: How long should an ad run before it's refreshed, weighing Meta's fatigue against the ad's own results?
areas.headline: Judge an ad by its own results, not its age. Long-runners that still hold their cost per chat and bookings keep their budget.

findings.text: 'failed hiko' has run 13 months (₱585k* lifetime) and still got ₱30.6* per chat in the last 30 days, at frequency 1.98.
'Drip 082124' has run 27 months and got ₱27.1* per chat in the last 30 days.
Meta groups lookalike ads as one creative (Andromeda), so new concepts need to be truly different, not small edits.

areas.recommendation: Weekly check per ad. Winner: if last 7 days cost per chat within +20% of its baseline AND at or under the ad set target, with bookings per chat holding, then keep running and keep its budget. Never edit it (an edit restarts learning); to try a change, duplicate it as a new ad. Tiring: if 2 of these in the last 7 days: cost per chat +20-35% over baseline, 7-day frequency above 2.5 (retargeting: above 5), CTR or hook rate (3-sec views / impressions) down 25%+ from its peak, quality ranking drops a level, then do not pause yet. Add 1-2 new versions to the same ad set (new first 3 seconds, new hook or new person, same core message) so Meta can shift spend. Fatigued: if cost per chat more than 35% over baseline for 2 weeks in a row, OR bookings per chat down 30%+ for 2 weeks, then pause it and launch its remake. Rest it 6-8 weeks, then it can come back as a new ad. Loser: if after 7 days and ₱3,000* spend: cost per chat 50%+ over the ad set target, or 0 bookings from its chats, then pause. It was never a winner, so no remake; learn from its hook.
areas.next: Built into the advisor's weekly moves.
